page.layout: One page of text in one column. Page number top left, running head top centre. No marginal notes. Catchword "bile" alone at the right below the last line.

main_text.p: veritatis &c. [illegible, ~12 letters] facto nos defectionis voluntaria crimine obstrin-gamus, Filium DEI conculcemus &c. idem Hebr. vi. Illi qui semel illuminati &c. τοὺς παραπίπτοντας[?] si prolabantur, si in peccata sua & apostasiam totalem & voluntariam recidant. IV. Utrobique eadem illis poena, idem exitium denunciatur, Petrus γεγονέναι αὐτοῖς τὸ ἔσχατον χείρονα τῶν πρώτων[?], κρεῖττον αὐτοῖς μὴ ἐπεγνωκέναι[?] &c. illis fuisse satius nunquàm nosse viam veritatis, dum isti ignorantiae accessit defectio, contumacia, rebellio: similiter Paulus Heb. x. οὐκ ἔτι περὶ ἁμαρτιῶν ἀπολείπεται θυσία[?], non hostiam, non sacrificium esse reliquum, nec in Christo, quae hostia nihil contumacibus, nihil incredulis, nihil impoenitentibus profit, nec extra Christum; adeo-que ubi non hostia, ibi nec expiatio, ubi non expiatio, ibi reatus, ubi reatus, ibi ira, ubi ira, ibi horrenda expectatio judicij, &c. Idem Heb. vi. ἀδύνατον πάλιν ἀνακαινί-ζειν εἰς μετάνοιαν, impossibile esse & ipsismet renovare sese per poenitentiam, & Do-ctoribus eosdem renovare, imo impossi-bile

page.notes: Greek words are partly garbled in the scan, especially the strikeout and overprint in the first line and the Greek in the Petrus and Heb. x. passages; the marked Greek is a best reading. The first line has overprinted or struck-through words around "facto nos" that could not be read with certainty. The running head reads as "De Authoritate Epistolae" but the middle letters are blurred.
